sections.title: Origins & History
sections.text: Pattadakal, on the banks of the Malaprabha River in Bagalkot district, Karnataka, was a ceremonial site where the Chalukya kings of Badami were crowned in the 7th and 8th centuries. The word Pattadakal means a place of coronation. The complex holds a remarkable group of temples built over about a century, and it is celebrated as a place where the architectural traditions of northern and southern India met and merged under royal patronage.

sections.title: Beauty & Atmosphere
sections.text: The beauty of Pattadakal comes from the variety and craftsmanship of the temples. Built of warm sandstone, they stand close to each other in a quiet landscape, with finely carved pillars, brackets, doorways and walls. Nine are Hindu temples, and one is a later Jain temple. Different styles can be seen side by side: the curved northern Nagara tower and the stepped southern Dravida tower, sometimes in the same structure.

sections.title: Architecture & Highlights
sections.text: The Virupaksha Temple, built around 740 by Queen Lokamahadevi to commemorate a victory over the Pallavas, is the grandest, with a great hall, tall pillars and carved scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas. The Mallikarjuna Temple, built by her sister queen, is of similar design. The Sangameshwara Temple is an earlier shrine, while the Papanatha Temple combines northern and southern ideas, and the Kashi Vishwanatha Temple is in the northern style. The Jain Narayana Temple dates to the later Rashtrakuta period.

sections.title: Famous For
sections.text: Pattadakal was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987, and is famous as an example of the fusion of architectural styles and of early Chalukya art. Along with nearby Badami and Aihole, it forms a cradle of temple architecture in India.

visitor_tips: Visitors should plan two to three hours at Pattadakal and combine it with Badami's cave temples and Aihole's early temples, usually in a day trip.
The cooler months, from October to February, are most comfortable.
Check opening times, ticket rules and any special restrictions with official sources before travelling.
